# Association Tool Selection Defaults

## Principle

Choose an association tool from the study design and requested output, not from
organism name alone. TASSEL and GEMMA are both species-agnostic in principle;
their common use patterns, supported formats, and model features make them
better fits for different requests.

## Default Routing

| Situation | Preferred starting path | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All-R simulated cohort, any species | `analyze_gwas()` plus `benchmark_gwas()` | Portable baseline with retained synthetic truth. |
| Plant/crop GWAS, HapMap/GBS/TASSEL output, LD/PCA/kinship workflow | TASSEL | Common crop-genetics ecosystem and plant-oriented data handling. |
| Plant GWAS explicitly comparing FarmCPU, BLINK, MLM, or GAPIT models | GAPIT/FarmCPU | Model comparison with identical input QC and causal truth. |
| Animal/human quantitative trait, PLINK/BIMBAM, LMM/mvLMM/BSLMM request | GEMMA | Efficient external mixed-model toolkit with relatedness-aware models. |
| Large human case-control or biobank-scale study | Ask for sample size, imbalance, ancestry, and compute environment | Do not silently default to GEMMA; tool choice may require other specialized methods. |
| Admixed/local-ancestry GWAS | RFMix/Tractor/GENESIS boundary plus explicit reference panels | Ordinary GWAS, admixture mapping, and local-ancestry association are distinct analyses. |

## Required Harmonization Before Comparing Tools

- Same sample manifest, genome build, marker coordinates, and allele coding.
- Same MAF/missingness/variant filters.
- Same phenotype transform, covariates, PCs, and relatedness treatment where comparable.
- Same simulated causal truth and recovery window for benchmark metrics.

## Required Outputs and Figures

- Per-tool command/configuration manifest and version.
- Filtered input summary, association tables, Manhattan and QQ plots.
- Synthetic-truth precision/recall/power comparison where truth exists.
- Explicit note when an external tool was planned but not executed locally.

## Guardrails

No species label alone determines the correct GWAS method. A default is a
starting recommendation to be confirmed with phenotype type, cohort size,
relatedness, ancestry, marker density, experimental design, and requested
analysis output.
